Final schema 3 qualification — 2026-10-19

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-tools-components-schema3-validation.Rmd
contributor-tools-components-schema3-validation.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

Supporting record: claims apply to the revisions and environments named below; this page does not qualify a later candidate.

Implementation commit: 6b1bee05a3fbb922415dc3774c63add2ad2a6b08. The package source manifest, tarball checksum, commands, logs and numerical snapshots are in validation/. The earlier schema 2 evidence is preserved separately; these checks were run on the final typed schema 3 code.

Check Newly executed result
R CMD build . Passed, including vignette generation.
R CMD check --no-manual --no-build-vignettes Status: OK, including examples, installed-package tests and vignette R code. Manual PDF generation and rebuilding vignette outputs during check were not run.
Source test suite 181 cases, 4,848 expectations; 0 failures/errors/warnings/skips.
Installed-package test suite 4,848 passed; 0 failures/warnings/skips.
BiocCheck 1.47.26 0 errors, 1 warning, 6 notes. R-version recommendation and interactive bioc-help check disabled.
Scientific/reference comparison Seven workflows, 231 tolerance-zero comparisons, all equal with matched realized budgets.
Optional dependency loading Package load, real schema 1 in-memory migration/access and closed descriptor inspection leave ondisc unloaded.
Final integration review No additional material public-path correctness issue found.

Environment: R 4.6.0, macOS arm64, ondisc 1.2.0. BiocCheck’s warning is the existing absence of Bioconductor infrastructure dependencies. Its six notes concern console output, condition-message construction, nonlocal assignment in the migration stage helper, function length, line width and indentation. These are recorded rather than claimed fixed. An initial sandboxed BiocCheck attempt could not acquire its metadata-cache lock; the completed run used authorized cache/network access.

The seven deterministic workflows cover low/high MOI, NT/complement controls, permutation/CRT, skew-normal/empirical tails, and union/Bonferroni/singleton integration. Comparisons include actual calibration/power/discovery tables, available numerical preparation payloads, compact response-fit payloads, warnings and R RNG state. The reference is the archived installation of 97d95da152dbf685e9f4664db7c302844cabe42e; it was not rebuilt in this pass. Its numerical code is unchanged. The reference driver restores the pre-calibration QC budget for discovery/power to match the established corrected policy; this does not claim equality to the legacy calibration-budget overwrite. Intentional schema/lifecycle differences and absent empty table placeholders are excluded. Raw candidate/reference observations and comparison scripts are preserved. Native statistical sources have no changes.

Tests cover real physical schema 1 and 2 fixtures, historical results and unknown provenance, canonical versus compiled pair ownership and multiplicity, stage and result invalidation, failed reruns, compact fit validation/reuse, source/analysis coordinates, backing save/reopen/relocation/wrong-file identity and response IDs that differ from display labels. Current field tables are reflected directly from S4 definitions; missing or stale field descriptions fail generation.

Active backing files are immutable during analysis; routine getters/reporting do not monitor external mutations. Qualification is local to this Mac and the recorded dependency versions. It establishes neither all historical-RDS compatibility nor large-screen performance, hosted CI or Linux/Windows behavior. Nextflow adaptation, push, PR publication, merge and release were not performed.

Developed by Timothy Barry, Louis Deutsch, Eugene Katsevich, Wharton Analytics, National Science Foundation.
